rules.pickup_tangent_constraint: applies to loose pickup poses, not to subsequent contact-constrained insertion poses
rules.support_continuity: Right holds the connector throughout pin insertion. Acquire left base/connector support before right releases it to fetch the upper arm. Preserve left support through upper-arm installation. Establish right support of the installed upper-arm piece before left releases its prior support to fetch the final module. Any grip relocation requires an explicit supported transition.
rules.terminal_examples: reference-only, excluded from training reset candidates
rules.reward: Fully seated is the completion target; entry/half/near must remain nonterminal. Exact tolerances and reward implementation require physical qualification.
rules.pin: vertical shaft downward at hole; halfway and near-seated are separate states
rules.variation: After nominal grasp/contact/clearance qualification, coherent variation within each family; do not randomize support arms independently.
rules.supported_insertions: In states 21-24 and 29-32 the far side remains in real surface contact with the receiver edge while the held servo is aligned with the receiving pocket. The upper-arm case is directed down into its base/connector pocket. The final-piece case follows the installed upper-arm receiver frame, which is tilted in world coordinates. Fold/tilt is derived from those contacts and mating constraints, not from preset world angles.
rules.servo_pickup_orientation: Keep the approved object orientation in states 18 and 19. Both fingers pinch the exposed black case faces shown in IMG_1612, with one finger in the open link window and the other outside the servo end. A grasp on the printed yoke is not an acceptable substitute. Loose-placement yaw and the actual finger-closure face normal are recorded separately.
rules.boundary_review: Check both fingers, palm and wrist camera against the grasped part and surrounding assembly in every updated state, especially state 25. Report rejected poses; an IK center residual or coarse SDF clearance alone does not establish a valid grasp.
rules.photo_evidence: Images establish qualitative pose, visible contact and both-arm roles. Exact insertion fractions, completion, loads, grasp forces and camera calibration are not measured by these photographs.

qualification.current: review-candidate authoring and geometric checking; no physical training admission
required: registered receiving-pocket and slide frames, far-end contacts and actual pin hole
reachable joint poses with the approved object orientations preserved in states 18/19
two opposed finger contacts on the intended black case, exterior cover walls, connector sides or upper pin cylinder
per-state finger, palm, wrist-camera, arm/link, table and surrounding-assembly boundary checks with current model/state identities
far-end resting contact and receiver-relative servo alignment throughout states 21-24 and 29-32
loaded grasp retention, receiver stability and continuous assembly support during both handoffs
entry, partial and near-seated starts remain nonterminal under the actual reward
bounded-action rollout and fine-step insertion validation before training admission

native_jaw_frame.asymmetric_gap_center: measured from fixed and moving jaw mesh sections

forearm_module.alignment: relative to the tilted upper-arm receiving pocket, not world vertical

support_holds.left_after_pin: photo-matched hold on the base/connector assembly, preserved throughout upper-arm installation and clear of its far-end resting edge
support_holds.right_after_upper: photo-matched hold on the installed upper-arm piece, preserved throughout final-piece installation and clear of the incoming module
support_holds.continuity: keep the assembly supported during any change of grasp; do not infer that one specific CAD axis or one unverified rail point is mandated by the photos
